en.title: Tarantino Has Tenth Film Script Ready, But Play Comes First
en.summary: Quentin Tarantino has confirmed a script for his final film is complete, but fans will have to wait. The legendary director plans to focus on his new play before returning to the silver screen.
en.body:
The maestro of modern cinema, **Quentin Tarantino**, has long promised that his tenth film would be his last. Now, in a candid appearance on *The Graham Norton Show*, he’s revealed that the script for this monumental, swan-song project is *already* written. However, before we can even dream of seeing this final chapter unfold, Tarantino is embarking on a different artistic venture: his new play, “**The Popinjay Cavalier**.”

> "I’ve written a script that I really like, but I want to do the play and see who I am; then I’ll then go back and spend time with my family and live a little and then see what I want to do." — **Quentin Tarantino**

This statement confirms what many fans have been eagerly anticipating. The script for his tenth film is complete, a significant milestone that suggests the wheels are turning, albeit slowly. However, Tarantino’s intention to prioritize his theatrical endeavor, which is set to open in March, before revisiting his cinematic plans, highlights a deliberate and thoughtful approach to his career's endgame. It’s a chance for him to explore a different creative outlet and, as he puts it, to “live a little” and reconnect with his family before diving back into the demanding world of filmmaking for what he’s stated will be his final directorial effort.

## The Road to Retirement

For cinephiles worldwide, the prospect of **Tarantino**’s tenth film carries immense weight. His filmography, including masterpieces like **Pulp Fiction**, **Inglourious Basterds**, and **Once Upon a Time in Hollywood**, has redefined cinematic storytelling for decades. Each film is a meticulously crafted event, brimming with his signature dialogue, unforgettable characters, and a deep reverence for film history. The confirmation of a completed script for his final movie is precisely the kind of news that sends ripples through the fan community, sparking endless speculation about plot, cast, and style. Will it be an original story, or will it delve into the worlds of his previously hinted-at projects, like a potential **Reservoir Dogs** sequel or a Western?

## What This Means for Fans

The immediate implication for fans is patience. While the script is ready, **Tarantino**’s commitment to his West End play, “**The Popinjay Cavalier**,” starring **Sacha Baron Cohen**, means a significant delay before pre-production or filming can even begin. This isn't just about a director taking a break; it’s about an artist consciously choosing to experience other facets of his craft and life before embarking on what is likely to be his most scrutinized film. The anticipation surrounding his final directorial outing is already palpable, and this period of reflection and theatrical exploration only adds layers to that excitement. It’s a testament to his dedication to his art that he’s willing to take this deliberate pause, ensuring that his final cinematic act is as considered and impactful as all the ones that came before.

## What's Next

With “**The Popinjay Cavalier**” slated to open in March, **Tarantino**’s focus will be on its theatrical run. Details regarding when he will officially return to his tenth film project, or any potential casting or plot points, have not yet been announced. Fans will be eagerly awaiting further updates following the play's conclusion, as **Tarantino** himself indicated he will reassess his plans then.
